bands.name: Anterior sacroiliac ligament

attachments.landmark_b: anterior margin of the iliac articular surface

bands.mechanical_role: a thin anterior capsular thickening; the sacroiliac joint's weakest ligamentous restraint
bands.function_note: Thin and membranous compared to the massive posterior/interosseous ligaments -- consistent with the SI joint's load-transfer mechanism relying primarily on its posterior structures.
bands.source: Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

function: A relatively weak anterior capsular thickening of the sacroiliac joint, in marked contrast to the much stronger posterior sacroiliac ligamentous structures.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

bands.name: Posterior/interosseous sacroiliac ligament

attachments.landmark_a: sacral tuberosity, deep to the posterior ligament

bands.mechanical_role: the primary load-transfer structure of the sacroiliac joint, resisting separation of the sacrum from the ilium under trunk/lower-limb loading
bands.function_note: Massive and among the strongest ligamentous structures in the body -- fills the deep interosseous space between the sacral and iliac tuberosities and is considered the SI joint's principal stabilizer, functionally continuous with the posterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia and the sacrotuberous ligament in Vleeming's self-locking force-closure model.
bands.source: Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

function: The sacroiliac joint's primary stabilizing structure, central to Vleeming's force-closure model of load transfer between spine and lower limbs.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

attachments.landmark_a: posterior sacrum and coccyx, lateral margins

bands.name: Sacrotuberous ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists nutation-related and axial-load-related sacral displacement; tensioned indirectly by biceps femoris and gluteus maximus, which partly blend into it
bands.function_note: Receives direct fibrous contributions from gluteus maximus and (via the falciform process) the long head of biceps femoris, giving those muscles an indirect dynamic influence over SI joint stability -- a myofascial coupling of the same kind documented for the thoracolumbar fascia's posterior layer.
bands.source: Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

function: A broad posterior pelvic ligament linking the sacrum/coccyx to the ischial tuberosity, reinforced dynamically by gluteus maximus and biceps femoris.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Vleeming A, Schuenke MD, Masi AT, Carreiro JE, Danneels L, Willard FH (2012) 'The sacroiliac joint: an overview of its anatomy, function and potential clinical implications.' J Anat 221(6):537-567 -- SI joint ligamentous stabilization, interosseous ligament as primary load-transfer structure.

attachments.landmark_a: lateral sacrum/coccyx (anterior to sacrotuberous ligament's origin)

bands.name: Sacrospinous ligament
bands.mechanical_role: together with the sacrotuberous ligament, converts the greater and lesser sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina
bands.function_note: Lies deep/anterior to the sacrotuberous ligament, crossing it in an X-shape; the sciatic nerve, pudendal nerve, and piriformis all pass through the foramen this ligament helps define, making it a key landmark in pelvic and gluteal surgical anatomy.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Divides the greater sciatic notch from the lesser sciatic foramen, a key anatomical landmark for the neurovascular structures exiting the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Superior pubic ligament
bands.mechanical_role: reinforces the superior aspect of the pubic symphysis
bands.function_note: Spans the superior symphyseal margin from one pubic tubercle to the other.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Reinforces the pubic symphysis superiorly, resisting separation of the two pubic bones.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Arcuate pubic ligament
bands.mechanical_role: a thick arch reinforcing the pubic symphysis inferiorly, forming the apex of the pubic arch
bands.function_note: Thicker and mechanically more substantial than the superior pubic ligament; its integrity is what allows the symphysis to resist shear during single-leg-stance gait loading.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The thick, mechanically dominant inferior reinforcement of the pubic symphysis, forming the apex of the subpubic arch.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Anterior band

attachments.landmark_a: anterior/inferior aspect of L5 transverse process

bands.mechanical_role: anchors the L5 transverse process to the ilium, limiting flexion/extension and axial rotation at the lumbosacral junction
bands.function_note: Per cadaveric dissection, the ligament consists of two parts (anterior and posterior), both arising from the L5 transverse process; contrary to older descriptions of a 3-5 part ligament inserting on the iliac crest, both parts were found to insert onto the upper iliac tuberosity, distinctly lower than the iliac crest, and neither part attaches to L4.
bands.source: Hanson P, Sonesson B (1994) 'The anatomy of the iliolumbar ligament.' Arch Phys Med Rehabil 75(11):1245-1246, doi:10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2 (https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2) -- cadaveric dissection establishing the two-part (anterior/posterior) structure of the iliolumbar ligament, both parts from L5 transverse process to iliac tuberosity.

bands.name: Posterior band

attachments.landmark_a: posterior/superior aspect of L5 transverse process
attachments.landmark_b: upper part of iliac tuberosity, posterior to the anterior band

bands.mechanical_role: together with the anterior band, stabilizes the L5 vertebra against the ilium, resisting excessive lumbosacral flexion, lateral bending, and rotation
bands.function_note: The stronger and more consistently identified of the two bands in cadaveric series; a common structural culprit implicated as a pain generator in the differential diagnosis of lower back and sacroiliac-region pain ('iliolumbar syndrome').
bands.source: Hanson P, Sonesson B (1994) 'The anatomy of the iliolumbar ligament.' Arch Phys Med Rehabil 75(11):1245-1246, doi:10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2 (https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2) -- cadaveric dissection establishing the two-part (anterior/posterior) structure of the iliolumbar ligament, both parts from L5 transverse process to iliac tuberosity.

function: Anchors the L5 transverse process to the ilium, stabilizing the lumbosacral junction and limiting excessive motion between the fifth lumbar vertebra and the pelvis; a well-established structure and a recognized differential consideration in lower-back and sacroiliac-region pain.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Hanson P, Sonesson B (1994) 'The anatomy of the iliolumbar ligament.' Arch Phys Med Rehabil 75(11):1245-1246, doi:10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2 (https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-9993(94)90013-2) -- cadaveric dissection establishing the two-part (anterior/posterior) structure of the iliolumbar ligament, both parts from L5 transverse process to iliac tuberosity.
